title: PII – Personally Identifiable Information
content: PII refers to any data that can identify a specific individual, directly or indirectly. At Nexum Financial S.A., PII includes: full name, national ID number, passport number, home address, email address, phone number, IP address when combined with other identifiers, biometric data, and financial account numbers. All PII must be classified Confidential or higher and processed strictly in accordance with POL-003 and GDPR. PII must be pseudonymised before use in analytics environments. Any accidental disclosure of PII must be reported to the DPO within 24 hours.

title: Data Lineage
content: Data lineage is the complete documentation of a data element lifecycle: origin, transformations applied, systems it passes through, and its final consumption point. Nexum Financial S.A. requires lineage documentation for all Tier-1 critical data assets. Lineage is captured in the enterprise data catalog and must be updated within 5 business days of any pipeline change. Automated lineage harvesting tools are used wherever possible. Lineage coverage is a key metric in the quarterly Data Governance maturity assessment. Breaking lineage gaps must be escalated to the CDO within 10 business days.

title: Data Steward
content: A Data Steward is an employee designated to oversee quality, governance, and proper use of specific data assets within their business domain. Core responsibilities include: approving data access requests, monitoring quality metrics, updating data definitions in the catalog, escalating governance violations to the CDO office, and participating in quarterly governance reviews. Each critical data domain must have at least one named Data Steward registered in the RACI matrix. Data Stewards must complete mandatory governance training annually. They have authority to freeze a dataset pending quality remediation.

title: Golden Record
content: A Golden Record is the single authoritative version of a data entity — such as a client, product, or counterparty — created by consolidating and deduplicating data from multiple source systems. The Master Data Management (MDM) platform produces golden records through survivorship rules. Only golden records from the MDM hub should be used in regulatory reporting and client-facing outputs to ensure data consistency. Survivorship rules are documented and version-controlled. Conflicts between source records must be resolved within 2 business days by the relevant Data Steward.

title: Data Mesh
content: Data Mesh is a decentralized data architecture paradigm where data ownership and responsibility are distributed to domain teams rather than centralized in a single data platform. Each domain treats its data as a product and exposes it via standardized data contracts with well-defined SLAs. At Nexum Financial S.A., the Data Mesh initiative is governed by the CDO office following a federated computational governance model with central policy enforcement. Domain data product owners are accountable for quality, availability, and discoverability. Self-serve infrastructure provided by the platform team enables domain teams to publish and consume data products without central bottlenecks.

title: CSSF Circular 12/552
content: CSSF Circular 12/552 is the Luxembourg financial regulator directive on central administration, internal governance, and risk management for supervised financial institutions. It mandates requirements for data governance frameworks including data quality controls, audit trails, and full documentation of data processing activities. Non-compliance may result in supervisory measures by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Compliance is assessed during annual supervisory reviews. Key requirements include: clear accountability for data assets, documented data flows, and an annual data governance self-assessment report.

title: DPIA – Data Protection Impact Assessment
content: A DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment) is a process required under GDPR Article 35 for processing activities that are likely to result in a high risk to individuals rights and freedoms. At Nexum Financial S.A., a DPIA is mandatory before deploying: new AI models processing personal data, large-scale profiling activities, systematic monitoring of employees, and processing of special categories of data. The DPIA must be conducted by the project team with support from the DPO. Results must be documented and retained for the duration of the processing plus 7 years. If residual risks remain high after mitigation, the CNPD must be consulted before processing commences.

title: BCBS 239 – Risk Data Aggregation Principles
content: BCBS 239 refers to the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting. It establishes 14 principles covering governance, data architecture, accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and adaptability. Nexum Financial S.A. applies BCBS 239 standards to all Tier-1 risk data assets. Key requirements include: a single authoritative source for each risk metric, automated aggregation with a documented lineage, and risk reports delivered to senior management within agreed SLAs. Self-assessments against BCBS 239 are conducted annually and submitted to the CRO and CDO.

title: Data Contract
content: A Data Contract is a formal, versioned agreement between a data producer and one or more data consumers that defines the structure, semantics, quality expectations, SLAs, and governance terms for a data product. At Nexum Financial S.A., all Tier-1 data interfaces must be governed by a data contract stored in the enterprise catalog. Contracts include: schema definition, field descriptions, data types, quality thresholds, refresh frequency, access restrictions, and change management procedures. Breaking changes require a 30-day deprecation notice. Contracts are reviewed annually or upon any material change to the underlying data pipeline.
